name: Tjaktja-Salka

difficulty.label: Moderate mountain pass stage; no formal official grade found
difficulty.source: STF gives no formal difficulty grade. Official and field sources describe a short but exposed stage over Tjaktjapasset, Kungsleden's highest point, with stony terrain, snow that can linger into July, scarce water near the pass and a steep/stony descent toward Salka.

notes: Official STF section direction is Tjaktja to Salka.
This is STF Abisko-Nikkaluokta stage 4 and the southern half of Naturkartan/Lansstyrelsen route BD31 Alesjaure-Salka.
The stage crosses Tjaktjapasset about 4 km south of Tjaktja. STF and Naturkartan describe this as Kungsleden's highest point at about 1150 m.
No ferry or boat belongs directly to this section. Boat services relevant to Alesjaure or Laddjujavri are adjacent access/stage-chain metadata, not section-4 route geometry.
Salka is a junction for the main Kungsleden south toward Singi and side routes toward Nallo and Hukejaure.

Stage is Tjaktja-Salka, 12 km, 3-5 hours.

campingRules.rule: No route-specific protected-area camping restriction was found in this batch. General allemansratten applies: short-term tenting is normally allowed when it does not disturb or damage; large groups or multi-night camps need landowner permission.

STF tent-fee policy applies near STF cabins when campers use cabin services. Hut-area tenting at Salka should be treated as access/service metadata unless exact official tent-zone coordinates are verified.

Field reports suggest camping can be possible in valley terrain, including near streams below/after the pass, but some hikers found fewer ideal sites close to Salka and wind exposure can be significant.

fireRules.rule: No route-specific fire ban was found. The Lanstyrelserna fire-ban layer reported no Kiruna municipal fire ban on 2026-04-29, but fire bans are volatile and must be checked day-of.
Tjaktjapasset shelter has a stove and firewood, but Naturkartan says firewood and overnight use are for emergencies. Do not model it as a normal fireplace.

rules.details: Norrbotten is reindeer-herding area. Dogs must be leashed or securely contained where reindeer are present and herding is allowed; 1 March-20 August requires especially strict control. Keep distance from reindeer, especially during April-June calving/small-calf period.

No Kiruna municipal fire ban was reported by the fire-ban layer on 2026-04-29. Fire bans can change quickly and must be checked day-of; the person lighting a fire remains responsible even without a ban.

No route-specific protected-area drone rule was found from the protected-area check. General Swedish drone rules still apply, including drone card/operator registration as applicable, 120 m open-category ceiling, avoiding uninvolved people, checking LFV Dronechart/NOTAM and possible Lantmateriet permission for spreading aerial imagery.

Current Lansstyrelsen small-game page covered 2025/2026 and ended 15 March 2026; next season was not confirmed in accessed pages. For late August/September 2026, recheck NatureIT/Lansstyrelsen open/closed hunting areas and avoid interfering with active hunts.
rules.caveat: The page had an apparent typo saying 16 September 2025-15 March 2025 while detailed terms indicated 15 March 2026.

currentness.details: No Tjaktja-Salka-specific bridge closure, reroute or broken-bridge notice was found on Lansstyrelsen current fjall pages as of 2026-04-29.

Lansstyrelsen's 2026-04-22 warning says winter route checks stopped because unsafe snow/ice conditions developed; old markers may remain on unsafe ice and streams may be open. This is a seasonal winter/spring warning, not a summer closure.

currentness.item: No 2026 summer snow report found yet
currentness.details: The latest route-specific STF snow report found was 2025-07-08, not 2026. It reported continuous snow over Tjaktja Pass and about 1 km south at that time.
currentness.confidence: high for absence in this pass; high for dated 2025 context

currentness.details: STF Tjaktja and STF Salka 2026 staffed periods are 20 February-19 April and 18 June-13 September. Between those dates, plan as unsupported except for emergency/safety spaces where available.

safetyNotes: Tjaktjapasset is exposed and stony, with potentially persistent snow into early July and a steep/stony descent south of the pass.
Water can be scarce around Tjaktjapasset; fill before the pass and treat/filter water near huts or high-use areas as needed.
Snowmelt and heavy rain can raise streams quickly; check SMHI warnings and local conditions.
Neither endpoint has direct public transport or road access. Evacuation and support options are limited.
Salka has shop/resupply while Tjaktja has no shop; shop selection can vary and may be limited after peak events or late in season.

conditionReports.sourceName: Outdoorsy Girl: Hiking the Kungsleden: Abisko, Alesjaure, Tjaktja, Salka
notes: Strong early-season warning: wind/rain before the pass, slushy ascent, melting snow and hidden summer-route markers after Tjaktja hut.
Hiker switched to winter-route markers in places; descent to Salka had excellent views and meltwater rivers.
Camping became harder near Salka and the hiker camped by the river near/beyond the hut.
conditionReports.importImpact: Add early-season pass snow/meltwater/hidden-marker warning and camping caveat near Salka.

conditionReports.sourceName: Reddit r/Kungsleden: Situation on the Kungsleden
notes: Between Tjaktja and Salka there was lots of snow, with about 3.5 km snowfield reported.
Wet feet were expected between Alesjaure and Salka; sun protection/sunglasses were important on snow.
conditionReports.importImpact: Supports late-June/early-July snow and wet-foot caution; do not mark as closure.

conditionReports.sourceName: Reddit r/Kungsleden: Travel options and other questions

sourceContradictions.details: STF publishes Tjaktja-Salka as a 12 km stage, while Naturkartan official county linework is a combined 25 km Alesjaure-Salka route that must be reversed and split. OSM relation 10861494 is section-specific but not official.

sourceContradictions.details: STF hut coordinates do not always coincide with OSM/Naturkartan stage-boundary geometry. Tjaktja is 220-328 m from line/stage coordinates; Salka aligns closer but Naturkartan's Salka-side endpoint is about 199 m from the hut.
sourceContradictions.impact: Do not snap route endpoints to hut centroids without verified spur geometry. Keep hut POIs and route geometry distinct.

agents.summary: Confirmed official STF stage 4 Tjaktja-Salka, 12 km and 3-5 hours, Tjaktjapasset high-point description, STF Tjaktja/Salka coordinates/services and Naturkartan shelter evidence.
Found OSM relation 10861494 as explicit section geometry and confirmed Naturkartan site 12865 is official combined Alesjaure-Salka linework requiring reverse/split; documented endpoint gaps.
Identified STF Tjaktja, Tjaktjapasset rest shelter/latrine, bridge before Salka and STF Salka as main facility records; flagged OSM-only child amenities and campsites for pending/suppression.
Confirmed no direct road/transit/boat access to Tjaktja or Salka; Abisko and Nikkaluokta are practical but distant multi-day access points.
Collected 2023-2025 field reports emphasizing early-season snow/meltwater/hidden markers at Tjaktjapasset, rocky/exposed pass terrain, water/camping caveats and Salka resupply pressure.
Found no section-specific closure/reroute/protected-area overlap in checked sources; documented 2026 winter-route warning, fire/dog/reindeer/hunting/drone caveats and lack of 2026 summer snow report.
